_meta.notes: Book gives no fixed per-muscle landmark tables; volume is individualized via the MEV estimator + set progression algorithm below.

principle_priority._note: Specificity is the most important; variation is a refinement once the rest are in place

effective_ranges._note: Intermediate-lifter ranges; large individual and training-age differences

rom.rule: Use a range that gives a notable stretch on the target muscle and goes as far as is safe; if the limb can travel further under load, use it

mesocycle.load_progression: add only enough load to repeat last week's reps at the same or slightly lower RIR
mesocycle.rep_progression: add only enough reps to keep last week's load at the same or slightly lower RIR

mev_estimator.when: first session(s) of a mesocycle, per muscle

score_bands.meaning: at or just above MEV (ideal start)
between MAV and MRV, maybe above MRV

inputs.soreness_0_to_3: 0 none; 1 mild, gone by next session; 2 DOMS healed just in time; 3 DOMS still present at next session
inputs.performance_0_to_3: 0 beat target by 2+ reps; 1 beat target by 0-1 reps; 2 needed to go past target RIR; 3 couldn't match last week
inputs._note: Average across all sets of the exercise; score week 1 performance as 1-2

set_progression.rule_override: Performance score >= 2 never adds sets; score 3 triggers fatigue management

recovery_session.scope: target the lagging muscle; whole session if large muscles/systemic fatigue

deload.trigger: MRV hit on multiple muscles, repeated MRV cycling, or RIR at 1-0; early is better than late
deload.first_half: same loads, half the sets and reps
deload.second_half: half the sets, reps, and load

fatigue_management.best_fatigue_indicator: performance (sequential drops or drops alongside other signs)

indices.RSM: maximize when recovery and time are fine but growth is lagging
indices.SFR: maximize when recovery is the limiter
indices.STR: maximize when time is the limiter
indices.SFTR: overall: growth vs fatigue and time

exercise_selection.rotate: between mesocycles based on staleness, pain, and performance

phase_potentiation.within_block: early mesos: heavier, lower frequency, lower volume; later mesos: higher volume and frequency, lighter loads
phase_potentiation.mev_mrv_drift: both rise by a few sets/week across a block
phase_potentiation.between_blocks: short low-volume maintenance phase at MV, low frequency, to resensitize

diet_phase_coupling.gain: MV and MEV fall, MRV rises; more high-RSM exercises are affordable
diet_phase_coupling.cut: MEV rises, MRV falls; intermediates/advanced gain ~no muscle, so stay near MEV (esp. late cut) and extend the meso with smaller set additions rather than shortening it
diet_phase_coupling.maintenance: low-volume work improves efficiency; good place for high-RSM exercises

training_age.beginner: technique focus, lower volume, few compound exercises covering lots of muscle
training_age.advanced: higher volume and possibly frequency, more specific exercises, tighter fatigue management, specialization phases (non-priority muscles at MV-MEV)
